html:
The Chatino are an Indigenous people of the southern mountains and Pacific slope of Oaxaca, Mexico. They call themselves Kitsé Cha'tnio. Their languages belong to the Zapotecan branch of the Oto-Manguean family, close to that of the Zapotec.

They farmed maize, beans and squash on steep slopes. Before the Spanish came, their country lay under the Mixtec kingdom of Tututepec on the coast, part of the wider Mixtec world, which resisted the Aztecs. Spanish conquerors reached the area in 1522.

Coffee growing spread into their mountains in the late 1800s and drew many Chatino into work on plantations. The shrine of the Virgin of Juquila in their land is one of the most visited pilgrim sites in southern Mexico.
